title: Verb in URL — POST /createUser violates REST resource naming
expected_feedback: Hygiene tier, item 1, nature [D], no live trigger — §8.1 makes this a **WARN**, so H1 is reported but not failed: URL contains a verb ('createUser'). REST resources are nouns — the HTTP method IS the verb; POST /api/v1/createUser should be POST /api/v1/users. This makes the API unpredictable (is it /getUser, /fetchUser, /retrieveUser?) and complicates OpenAPI tooling that expects resource-based paths. Naming is a convention, not a protocol requirement. Two consequences to state in the report: it belongs in the Hygiene tier, not Critical; and because no risk trigger is live, §8.1 scores it WARN — H1 still passes. It would only become a FAIL if the deviation were also inconsistent across the API under a live trigger. Standard tier, item 2, nature [P] — §8.1 makes any invariant violation a **FAIL**, so S1 fails: the genuine protocol defect in this snippet is the response — a successful create returns 200 with no Location header instead of 201 Created plus Location pointing at the new resource. That one is not a matter of taste.
